prompt: Many developing countries have built their economies around large-scale international tourism. Do the advantages of this approach outweigh the disadvantages?
essay:
Several countries have made international tourism the centre of their development strategy rather than one component of it. In my view the advantages of doing so do outweigh the disadvantages, but only where the country retains some control over how the industry grows.

The economic argument is difficult to dismiss. Tourism produces foreign currency quickly, requires less initial capital than manufacturing, and creates work at every skill level, from construction to hotel management. Nor is the workforce a barrier: hotel and hospitality skills can be taught in months, whereas building a manufacturing base takes a generation. For a country with beaches or ruins and little else to export, it is often the only sector in which it starts with an advantage. The revenue is also visible: airport taxes, licensing and hotel levies are far easier to collect than income tax in a largely informal economy.

The disadvantages, though, are structural rather than incidental. Much of the money leaves again almost immediately, because international chains and foreign tour operators repatriate their profits, and an all-inclusive resort is designed so that guests spend nothing outside of it. Meanwhile the jobs available to local people cluster at the bottom, seasonal and poorly paid. Land prices near attractive coastlines rise beyond what residents can pay, and a monoculture economy is dangerously exposed: a single security incident or a change in fashion can empty a country's hotels for a year.

Even so, I would keep the judgement in tourism's favour, because the alternatives available to most of these economies are worse. Where governments have insisted on local ownership, capped development and taxed the sector properly, tourism has funded genuine improvements in infrastructure. The disadvantages are largely the result of how the industry is regulated, and regulation can be changed.
title: Mass tourism in developing economies
